blocks.content: A meteoroid becomes a meteor when entering the atmosphere and a meteorite upon reaching the Earth's surface.

Tail always points away from the Sun
Streak aligns with atmospheric entry path

items: Memorize the precise terminology shift: Meteoroid (space) -> Meteor (atmosphere/shooting star) -> Meteorite (ground surface).
Comet tails ALWAYS point directly away from the Sun due to solar radiation pressure and solar wind, regardless of the comet's travel direction.
Lonar Lake in Buldhana district, Maharashtra, is a frequently tested example of a meteorite impact crater in India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Asteroids are rocky, metallic objects orbiting the Sun, primarily located in the Asteroid Belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Comets are composed of frozen ice, dust, and rock; as they approach the Sun, solar radiation creates a glowing atmosphere (coma) and a tail.
Meteoroids are small rocky particles in space; upon entering Earth's atmosphere, friction burns them up, creating a bright streak of light called a Meteor.
A Meteorite is a meteoroid fragment that survives its passage through the atmosphere and strikes Earth's surface.
Ceres is the largest object in the main asteroid belt and is classified as a dwarf planet.
